subject: french
timingNote: Higher Level: the written paper is 2h 30m and 220 marks (55% of your grade): Section A reading comprehension 120 marks and Section B written production 100 marks. The Listening Comprehension (aural) is 80 marks, 40 minutes (20% of your grade), sat the same morning, and is the third section here. The Oral Examination is 100 marks (25% of your grade) and is held in March or April, so it is already behind you when you sit the paper. The three parts add to 400 marks. Ordinary Level splits differently: oral 80 marks (20%), aural 100 marks (25%), reading 160 marks (40%) and written 60 marks (15%). The marks and percentages for Higher Level are from the NCCA French syllabus and the SEC 2025 marking scheme. For the Oral Examination see the AAC guide called Oral Examination. 2027 dates are not published yet, and 2026 sat on Wednesday 10 June.

examDay.task: Wednesday 10 June in 2026, written paper 9:30 to 12:00 and the aural at about 12:10 to 12:50 after a short break (these aural times are from school summaries of the SEC timetable, not the SEC page itself). The 2027 timetable is not yet published. You get one answer booklet (your answers are written in the spaces provided and scanned for the examiner, so stay inside the boxes) and then the aural recording is played in the hall.
facts: Section A: both comprehensions. Section B: Question 1 is compulsory (a, b or c), then one of Questions 2 to 6. Nothing is optional in the aural.

French questions get French answers. The 'Do you agree?' questions (Q6, two points, about 50 words) get English or Irish. All the aural answers are in English or Irish: whole-test French answers lose 50% of the marks earned.

I found no new French specification or changed exam format announced for 2027. The 2025 and 2026 papers share the same layout, so use them as the model. Check your school notice and the SEC timetable when 2027 dates are issued.

Written paper is 2h 30m. Section A has four comprehensions at 40 marks each (160). Section B is two 30-mark tasks from six (filling gaps, form, message, postcard, diary, formal letter) for 60. Aural is five sections at 20 marks each (100).

timeline.label: Skim
timeline.detail: Read both texts quickly and the three Q1 options in Section B. Decide which Q1 you might write on.

timeline.label: Text 1
timeline.detail: Journalistic article. Ten 5-mark questions, then Q6 (two points in English or Irish).

timeline.label: Text 2
timeline.detail: Literary extract, same 60-mark shape. Harder: dialogue and implied meaning.

timeline.label: Q1 write
timeline.detail: Compulsory 60-mark piece, about 90 words. Plan 3 minutes, write 25, re-read 7.

timeline.label: Q2 to 6
timeline.detail: Diary, email or opinion, about 75 words, 40 marks.

timeline.label: Check
timeline.detail: Re-read for verb endings, agreement and accents. Check Q6 is in English or Irish.

timeline.label: Break
timeline.detail: Short break between the paper and the recording (reported times).

timeline.label: Aural
timeline.detail: Sections A to E, 80 marks, answers in English or Irish. Write in every pause.

tips.timing: About 35 minutes per text (70 in total, plus 5 to skim both texts and the Section B Q1 options). Each text carries 60 marks: ten 5-mark questions and a 10-mark opinion question. That is under 3 minutes a question once you have read the text.
tips.structure: Two texts, you answer both. Text 1 is a journalistic article (2025: scouting, from France Inter). Text 2 is a literary extract (2025: David Foenkinos, La famille Martin). Each text has Q1 to Q5 in two parts (a) and (b), then Q6 in Irish or English. Questions name the section of the text to look in, for example '(Section 2)'. Answer French questions in French and the Q6 opinion in English or Irish.
reminders: Answer in the language the question is asked in. The 2025 scheme takes 1 mark off any answer in the wrong language, including Q6 written in French
Each part is worth 5 marks. Partial marks run 4, 3, 2, 1 as you leave out pieces of the key phrase, so a half-right quote still scores
'Excess' is penalised: copying extra material beyond the answer loses 1 or 2 marks (marked EXC on scripts)
Section B Q1 gives three options that all refer back to these texts, so read both texts properly first and note which options you could write on
Write each part (a) and (b) on its own answer line. Two answers on one line count as one answer

questionTypes.name: Explain or quote an answer (question en français)
questionTypes.where: Q1 and Q2, parts 1(a), 1(b) and usually 4(b), 5(b). 2025 Text 1 Q1(a) 'pourquoi le scoutisme est-il de plus en plus populaire ?' and Text 2 Q1(b) 'Qui est-ce que l'auteur a vu en sortant de son immeuble ?'
questionTypes.see: A who, what or why question in French with the text section named. The scheme accepts a direct quotation or a correct manipulation (changing the verb or pronoun so the sentence fits your answer) on the parts it lists, for example 'Appropriate direct quotation OR correct manipulation acceptable'.
questionTypes.marked: 5 marks for the full phrase. 2025 Text 1 Q1(a): the full 'le désir pour un retour à la nature et à une vie en communauté' = 5, only 'retour à la nature' = 3, 'pour la nature' = 3. Naming only 'Les scouts' for Q1(b) got 2. Marks drop for each missing piece.
questionTypes.play: Find the sentence in the named section. Lift the whole phrase that answers the question, stop where the answer stops, and change the subject or verb only if the question needs it (Il a fondé le scoutisme).
traps: Quoting a whole sentence when a phrase is asked (a 'Full sentence' answer was capped at 3 marks in 2025 Text 1 Q2(a) and Q5(b))
Giving only one half of a two-part answer: 'nature' without 'vie en communauté' loses a mark
Using je when the question is about 'l'auteur': where manipulation is required, an unchanged 'je vis' copy loses a mark (2025 Text 2 Q1(b) 4 not 5)

questionTypes.name: Find a word, phrase or sentence
questionTypes.where: Q2 to Q5 in each text. 2025 Q2(b) 'Trouvez le mot qui veut dire « obtenir »' (acquérir) and Q4(a) 'Citez l'expression qui veut dire « des moments favorables et des moments difficiles »' (des hauts et des bas).
questionTypes.see: A vocabulary or style task. 'Trouvez / relevez le mot' means one word. 'Citez l'expression' means part of a sentence. 'Citez / relevez la phrase' means the whole sentence. You can also be asked for a grammar item, for example a passé composé verb (2025 Text 2 Q3(a): suis approché, a ralenti and ai expliqué were all accepted).
questionTypes.marked: 5 marks for the exact word or phrase, minus 1 for each extra word. 'D'acquérir' instead of 'acquérir' = 4. 'Des hauts' alone = 2 out of 5.
questionTypes.play: Match meaning in the named section, give just the word and stop. For a grammar item, scan the section for the tense marker (auxiliary plus past participle) and copy one clean example.
traps: Writing a whole line around the word: minus 1 for each extraneous element
Looking in the wrong section: the question names the section to search

questionTypes.name: Pronoun reference
questionTypes.where: 2025 Text 1 Q3(b) 'relevez le mot auquel le pronom les se réfère' (camps).
questionTypes.see: A pronoun (les, y, en, qui, leur) and a section to look in. You name the noun it stands for.
questionTypes.marked: 5 marks for the one correct noun ('camps'). 'La grande majorité des camps' = 1 out of 5.
questionTypes.play: Read back from the pronoun to the nearest matching plural or singular noun. Check gender and number, then write only that noun.
traps: Giving the whole noun phrase ('la grande majorité des camps'): 4 of the 5 marks go
Choosing the nearest noun without checking it agrees with the pronoun (les needs a plural)

questionTypes.name: Multiple choice
questionTypes.where: Q3(a) of Text 1, Q3(b) of Text 2 in 2025. A four-option tick box beginning 'Selon la troisième section...'.
questionTypes.see: Four statements, one correct. The wrong ones are usually the opposite of the text, or true of another section.
questionTypes.marked: 5 marks for one correct tick. If you tick more than one, 0. Clearly circling or underlining the right box is accepted in place of a tick.
questionTypes.play: Cross out the ones that contradict the section named, then check the survivor against the text. Never tick two.
traps: Ticking an option that is true of the whole text but not of the section named
Changing your mind and leaving two marks: more than one answer = 0

questionTypes.name: Opinion in English or Irish (Q6)
questionTypes.where: Q6 of each text. 2025 Text 1: 'Scouting has become attractive for young people in the 21st century. Do you agree?' Text 2: 'The elderly woman appears to be the ideal subject for the writer's new book. Do you agree?'
questionTypes.see: A statement, a request to refer to the text, and '(Two points, about 50 words in total)'. Written in English or Irish.
questionTypes.marked: Two points at 5 marks each. Any two valid points from the text count, whether you agree or disagree. The scheme lists around 20 agree points for Text 1 (membership nearly doubled from 75,000 to 130,000, long waiting lists, 200 euro for a fortnight at camp) and takes disagree points too (waiting lists, highs and lows, the cost).
questionTypes.play: Pick your side in one clause, then give two facts from the text. Two short sentences of about 25 words each.
traps: Writing Q6 in French: 1 mark penalty and no extra credit
Giving your own opinion with no reference to the text: the points have to come from the text
Spending time on a third point: only two are marked

tips.timing: About 35 minutes for Question 1 (60 marks, about 90 words) and 25 minutes for your Question 2 to 6 pick (40 marks, about 75 words). Keep the last 15 minutes of the paper to read both pieces through. Do Section A first: every Question 1 option points back to the two texts.
tips.structure: You answer two questions. Question 1 is compulsory: choose one of (a), (b) or (c) (2025: opinion on club membership, opinion on how we treat older people, or a story about a challenge). Then choose one of Questions 2 to 6 (2025: diary, email, and three opinion questions on drugs, gender inequality and youth in politics, with an image or quote as stimulus). Everything is written in French.
reminders: The marks split in half: Communication and Language. In Q1 that is 30 and 30, in Q2 to 6 it is 20 and 20
Word counts are 'environ' (about): 90 for Q1 and 75 for Q2 to 6. Do not go far over. The scheme penalises irrelevant material in Communication
In 2025 Q3 (email) no particular layout was required, and the marking sheet tracks points in the email (annotation P). Answer every question your friend asks
The 2026 paper's Section B was reported as vocabulary-hungry (fast fashion, a first driving lesson, AI, learning languages), so have 8 to 10 reusable topic phrases ready
Choose your Q2 to 6 task by vocabulary you already own, not by how interesting it sounds

questionTypes.name: Question 1 opinion piece (a) or (b)
questionTypes.where: Compulsory Question 1 every year. 2025 (a) 'est-ce qu'il est essentiel pour une jeune personne d'être membre d'un club ou d'une organisation ?' and (b) 'de nos jours, est-ce qu'on traite les personnes âgées avec assez de respect ?' 2026 options (press and teacher reports): travel, the housing crisis, a récit.
questionTypes.see: A link sentence to one of the Section A texts, then a question that asks for your opinion, with '(90 mots environ)'.
questionTypes.marked: 30 Communication plus 30 Language. Communication top band 20 to 30: stimulus well used, coherent, clear argument, little irrelevant material, few register mistakes. Middle 12 to 19, bottom 0 to 11. Language top band 20 to 30: idiomatic French, rich vocabulary, complex sentences handled well, few mistakes in verbs, agreement or spelling.
questionTypes.play: Opening line gives your position. Two reasons with an example each. Use a link word between them (d'abord, en outre, cependant). Finish with a one-line conclusion. Pull one idea or phrase from the Section A text to show you used the stimulus.
traps: Ignoring the stimulus: 'stimulus material well exploited' is the first Communication descriptor
A list of memorised sentences that does not answer the question asked: 'a lot of irrelevant material' drops you to the middle or bottom band
Tense errors in the main verbs: 'most verbs incorrect' is the bottom Language band

frequency.note: Question 1 changed from two options (one opinion, one story) to three in 2021, and Section B went from 3 pieces to 2 in 2021; I counted only the opinion options across all 13 papers because the task is the same. The (c) story option is not counted.

questionTypes.name: Question 1 narrative (c)
questionTypes.where: Option (c) in the 2025 paper: 'avez-vous déjà eu l'occasion de faire face à un défi ? Racontez ce qui s'est passé. (Votre récit peut être réel ou imaginaire.)' 2026: a récit about asking someone for a chance, which one teacher called 'a little odd' on the day.
questionTypes.see: A story prompt that the paper tells you can be real or invented, 90 words.
questionTypes.marked: Same 30 plus 30 grid. The Communication descriptors on coherence and clarity apply to a story as well: a clear beginning, middle and end.
questionTypes.play: Use passé composé for events and imparfait for background (il pleuvait, j'avais peur). Plan a three-sentence skeleton before you write. Invent facts you can say correctly.
traps: Mixing passé composé and imparfait at random: the examiner reads this as verbs generally wrong
Writing a 90-word story with no ending: coherence is a Communication descriptor

questionTypes.name: Diary entry (journal intime)
questionTypes.where: One of Questions 2 to 6. 2025 Q2: a party tomorrow and a red weather warning: 'Qu'est-ce que vous notez à ce sujet dans votre journal intime ?' 2026: a first driving lesson (reported as vocabulary-heavy).
questionTypes.see: A situation of 2 or 3 lines and the instruction to write in your journal, about 75 words.
questionTypes.marked: 20 Communication plus 20 Language. Communication top band 13 to 20, middle 8 to 12, bottom 0 to 7. Same Language descriptors as Q1 scaled to 20.
questionTypes.play: Date at the top, 'Cher journal', then feelings and a decision: je suis (adj), j'ai décidé de, il vaut mieux que. Finish with what you will do next.
traps: Writing as a third person or in a formal register: the grid lists 'mistakes in register'
Skipping the decision the question asks for (2025: cancel the party or not): the communicative intention is not fulfilled

questionTypes.name: Email or letter
questionTypes.where: 2025 Q3: an email to Mohammed or Nadia answering four questions about mobile phones in school. 2026 Q3 (Irish Times sample): an email answering four questions from a friend planning a trip to Ireland with a brother who uses a wheelchair.
questionTypes.see: A message from a friend with a list of four questions and '(75 mots environ)'. You reply as yourself.
questionTypes.marked: 20 plus 20. The 2025 scheme notes 'Q.3 - no particular layout required' and uses a points tally in the email, so each question you answer counts.
questionTypes.play: Greet, answer the four questions in order with one sentence each (reasons, not yes/no), close with a friendly line. Use tu with a friend.
traps: Answering three of the four questions: the missing point costs Communication marks
Switching to vous in the middle of an email to a friend

questionTypes.name: Opinion with image or quote
questionTypes.where: 2025 Q4 (cannabis statistic from Santé Publique France, drugs among Irish youth), Q5 (inequality between women and men), Q6 (quote from Euthyme Hessou on young people and politics, 'Qu'en pensez-vous ?'). 2026: fast fashion, artificial intelligence, learning foreign languages.
questionTypes.see: A short printed stimulus and a question, '(75 mots environ)'.
questionTypes.marked: 20 plus 20 on the same grid as the diary.
questionTypes.play: State your view in the first sentence, give two reasons and one example with a figure or fact from the stimulus, finish with a 'à mon avis' line. Subjonctif after il faut que (the 2025 Q6 quote has one) is cheap Language credit.
traps: Describing the picture and not answering the question
Copying phrases from the stimulus: the grid rewards your own language
Writing 130 words and running out of time on Question 1

frequency.note: Before 2021 these were the opinion options in Questions 3 and 4; since 2021 they are among Questions 4 to 6. A paper can count under more than one theme, and an option is counted under its main theme (some under two).

tips.timing: About 40 minutes, sat in the hall straight after the written paper (2025 and 2026 schedule reported 12:10 to 12:50 after a 10-minute break; 2027 times not yet published). The recording sets the pace. Use every pause to write and read the next question.
tips.structure: Five sections, A to E, 80 marks: A 12, B 21, C 18, D 21, E 8. Answers are in English or Irish. A to D are longer exchanges (2025: three holiday speakers, a postwoman interview, a conversation about pets and fish, a report on school uniforms) and E is a set of short news items. The marking scheme gives 3 marks per detail in A to D and 2 per detail in E.
reminders: Answer in English or Irish. If the whole test or a whole section is answered in French it is marked normally and then 50% of the marks gained are taken off
Where a question says 'two details', give two separate ones: each is 3 marks in sections A to D
Numbers need to be exact: in 2025 a wrong time or money amount (3 and a half hours, 300 euro) scored 0, and a wrong fine cost 1 mark
Section E is the hardest (every year report: it often hinges on one vocabulary item). Playing pattern reported by past guides is three plays for A to D and two for E: check what the tape says
Never leave a line blank: the scheme accepts any wording that communicates the point

questionTypes.name: Section A: three short personal accounts
questionTypes.where: Section A, 12 marks. 2025: Yves (why was he sad at the end of the holidays?), Zoé (two activities: surfing, windsurfing, diving), Luc (learned to ski).
questionTypes.see: Three speakers, short answer to each. One of them usually asks for two details.
questionTypes.marked: 3 marks per detail. Zoé: any two of surfing, windsurfing, (scuba) diving = 6. Yves: 'had to go back to Paris' = 3. If one of the two details is only half right, the scheme gives the higher mark to both (rule applied to A-2, C-2, D-1).
questionTypes.play: Write the question word in English (why, what, how long) in the margin so you know what to listen for. Jot down the answer in the first play and polish it in the second.
traps: 'Went home' alone is 2 of 3: say where, and why it was sad
Giving one detail where two are requested

questionTypes.name: Section B: interview
questionTypes.where: Section B, 21 marks. 2025: Elsa, a postwoman. Reasons she likes the job, who else she works with (people with disabilities), why she stops to talk to people living alone, how long she works in the morning (3 hrs 30), an afternoon activity (a homeless shelter).
questionTypes.see: Seven 3-mark items. Two are 'two details', two are single facts.
questionTypes.marked: 3 marks per correct detail, partial credit for half answers (shelter = 2). 'People' alone for who she works with = 0.
questionTypes.play: A job interview gives you who, where and when facts. Note numbers as digits and write one noun for each item you hear.
traps: Giving the wrong time or sum: 0
Answering with a generic word (people, job) instead of the specific one the speaker says

questionTypes.name: Section C: dialogue between two people
questionTypes.where: Section C, 18 marks. 2025: Laure and Vincent, a dog called Jazz (Laure is obsessed with jazz), and Vincent's fish collection (from all over the world, magnificent colours, a lot of work).
questionTypes.see: A phone-style conversation between friends. Questions go by speaker: what does Vincent say, why does he suggest she visits?
questionTypes.marked: 3 marks per detail; partial 2 or 1 for incomplete.
questionTypes.play: Keep track of who is speaking. Write Laure and Vincent at the top of your page and note one fact under each.
traps: Attributing Vincent's statement to Laure: the question names the speaker
'Music' for 'jazz' gets 0 in the scheme where the question asks why he is not surprised by the name

questionTypes.name: Section D: report with numbers and opinions
questionTypes.where: Section D, 21 marks. 2025: school uniforms in a French town (300 euro, paid by the state), how they reduce bullying, Clara's first impression, and when uniforms came to Ireland (at least a century ago).
questionTypes.see: Longer than the others: a report plus a student speaking. Includes two-part answers and one figure question.
questionTypes.marked: 3 marks per correct detail. Wrong amount of money = 0. A uniform paid for by the wrong source scored 1 mark, 'paid for / free' 2.
questionTypes.play: Listen once for the structure (who pays, what effect, what the student says) and the second time for the numbers.
traps: Hearing 'trois cents' and writing 30
Writing 'It reduces bullying' for the question 'how does it help': you need the mechanism (everyone looks the same, less jealousy)

questionTypes.name: Section E: news items
questionTypes.where: Section E, 8 marks. 2025: how criminals got into a pharmacy (broke the rear door), two on-the-spot penalties for a driver (driving ban and a 1,000 euro fine), why a tennis player was disqualified (he hit the umpire).
questionTypes.see: Three 2-mark news items (2025): one detail each, sometimes 'two of'.
questionTypes.marked: 2 marks per correct item; a wrong fine amount took 1 mark off; 'wrong person' took 1 off.
questionTypes.play: Read the questions before the news begins and listen for one noun per item. Vocabulary of crime, sport and weather appears often.
traps: Guessing the wrong person (the umpire, not the opponent)
Running out of time on the last item: this section moves fast and is played fewer times in older descriptions
